title: Length-smoothing scheduler with KV temporal reservation and slot-aging hysteresis
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: Problem: Mixed prompt/response length workloads (short prompts + long continuations and vice-versa) create pathological batching behavior: slot thrashing, excessive KV cache evictions, and p99 latency spikes. Goal: implement and tune a scheduler that smooths abrupt length heterogeneity, reduces KV eviction churn, and keeps short-turn latency within SLOs while preserving overall throughput and GPU memory efficiency. This ticket covers design, experiments, tuning knobs, and canary rollout for the Length-Smoothing Scheduler (LSS) with a KV temporal reservation layer and slot-aging hysteresis to avoid ping-ponging allocations.
acceptance_criteria: New scheduler integrated behind feature flag and enabled via per-route config
P99 tail latency for short-turn traffic reduced by >=20% versus baseline under mixed workload (measured on dedicated staging cluster)
KV cache eviction rate reduced by >=30% for mixed-length traces
GPU memory peak reduced or unchanged while maintaining throughput within 5% of baseline
Automated canary: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with rollback hooks and fallback to existing scheduler
design_decisions: Use per-slot exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) for observed sequence length to predict occupancy rather than instantaneous length
Implement transient KV temporal reservation: mark recently used KV entries with short TTL that prevents immediate eviction for predicted reuse windows
Introduce slot-aging hysteresis: slots recently vacated keep a low-cost reservation for a short aging window to enable coalescing of near-future prompts
Adaptive micro-slicing: allow splitting long responses across multiple contiguous micro-slots (soft partitioning) when it improves tail latency for interleaved short-turns
Latency budget parameter (ms) per route determines maximum batching window and micro-slice aggressiveness
implementation_plan: Prototype scheduler as pluggable strategy in runtime/scheduler/strategies
Add metrics and tracing hooks: per-slot length EWMA, KV temporal reservation hits/misses, slot-age histogram, eviction churn rate
Unit tests for reservation expiry, EWMA adaptation, and hysteresis correctness
Bench harness: replay mixed-length production traces in staging (short-heavy, long-heavy, and 50/50 interleaved) with adjustable token arrival patterns
Performance runs across GPU shapes (A10G, H100-like) to calibrate kernel selection interactions and memory footprint
experiment_plan: Baseline: current continuous-batcher with LRU KV eviction; run 1-hour traces for each workload mix
Treatment A: LSS with conservative EWMA alpha=0.25 and reservation_ttl=500ms
Treatment B: LSS aggressive EWMA alpha=0.6 and reservation_ttl=1200ms + micro-slicing enabled
Measure p50/p95/p99 latencies, KV eviction/sec, KV hit rate, throughput (tokens/sec), GPU memory peak and fragmentation metrics
Run 10 repeated trials and use paired analysis to control noise; capture failure modes where micro-slicing increases overall tokenization overhead
metrics_and_targets: Short-turn p99 latency target: reduce by >=20% from baseline (example baseline: 180ms -> target <=144ms)
Overall throughput: within -5% to +5% of baseline
KV hit rate: absolute increase >=5 percentage points on mixed traces
GPU peak memory: not to exceed baseline +2% for safety; prefer reductions
tradeoffs_and_risks: Reservation TTL too long -> increased memory retention and possible OOM in extreme tail; mitigated by tight upper bound and global memory pressure signal
EWMA too slow -> fails to adapt to rapid turn-length shifts; too fast -> reintroduce thrash. Will tune via experiments
Micro-slicing adds scheduler complexity and small tokenization overhead; may harm throughput for highly homogeneous long workloads. Will gate micro-slicing by heterogeneity score and latency budget
Slot-aging hysteresis could delay packing efficiency under sustained low-latency small-turn traffic; apply decay factor based on observed arrival rates
rollout_plan: Feature flag behind per-customer route: runtime.feature.length_smoothing
Canary 5% of traffic for 48h with automatic rollback if p99 increases >5% or evictions grow >15%
If stable, escalate to 25% for 72h then 100% with staged ramp and post-rollout verification
Provide operator knobs in Console (batching.window_ms, kv.reservation_ttl_ms, ewma.alpha, micro_slicing.enabled) and presets for common profiles
testing_checklist: Unit tests for EWMA and hysteresis boundary conditions
Integration test: replay recording that previously caused OOM under old scheduler; ensure no OOM with LSS
Perf suite: end-to-end replay on dedicated staging cluster (H100) with detailed per-token traces
Chaos test: simulate transient GPU memory pressure and verify reservation TTL honors global reclaim signals
